ideas.title: Refine the generic “Preserve Editorial Intent” guard into a constrained, context-aware Narrative rule
ideas.description: Replace the single, generic preservation paragraph with a narrowly scoped guard that (a) explicitly preserves company-level primary message and intended audience primacy, (b) treats technical explanations (e.g., orchestration) as subordinate unless the Synthesis unambiguously elevates them, and (c) forbids introducing new audiences, commitments, or validation claims. Ship this change together with a focused test harness that validates the hierarchy against the saved baseline/candidate outputs and the experiment scoring rubric.
ideas.audience: Prompt engineers, Narrative/Compose owners, and content/QA engineers working on Nueyon.Compose prompt and output pipelines
ideas.rationale: The candidate prompt added a single, generic preservation instruction but produced stable regressions: it systematically subordinated the company identity and audience while elevating orchestration and also introduced unsupported audience/validation claims. A constrained, context-aware guard plus verification against experiment artifacts is the most direct editorial fix indicated by the experiment.
ideas.evidence: Artifact and failure traces exist: the candidate prompt diff is saved (`prompt-changes/Narrative.user.prompt.diff`), full outputs and logs are archived (`baseline/outputs/` and `candidate/outputs/`), and the scoring rubric and run scores show the regressions.

ideas.title: Add automated editorial-fidelity checks to the pipeline
ideas.description: Implement rule-based checks that run after Narrative output: (1) detect demotion of company identity vs. product positioning, (2) flag newly introduced audience labels or commitments, and (3) detect when a supporting theme (like orchestration) becomes the central message. Surface diagnostics to editors and require human review before Compose proceeds when checks trigger.
ideas.audience: Pipeline engineers, QA, and prompt owners
ideas.rationale: The experiment shows human-evaluated scoring consistently identified fidelity regressions; rule-based checks would catch obvious violations earlier and prevent propagation to Compose outputs.
ideas.evidence: Use the saved baseline/candidate outputs, the prompt diff, and the experiment rubric as test vectors and thresholds.

ideas.title: Resolve the Synthesis internal tension by clarifying source hierarchy
ideas.description: Edit the Synthesis/source input to remove or disambiguate mixed signals (for example, the later line calling orchestration “central to the product direction”) so the source itself presents a clearer top-level hierarchy before Narrative runs.
ideas.audience: Content authors and product communicators who draft Synthesis/source inputs
ideas.rationale: The report notes that the baseline Synthesis pairs company identity with Compose at top-level but later calls orchestration central; that internal tension likely contributed to model prioritizing orchestration. Clarifying the source reduces ambiguity for Narrative.
ideas.evidence: The experiment report observes the baseline Synthesis contains a later description calling orchestration “central to the product direction,” and suggests that internal tension may have reinforced the technical angle.

grounding.claim: A ‘Preserve Editorial Intent’ rule already exists in the candidate prompt and is the locus for refinement.
grounding.sourceEvidence: The candidate added one generic section, **“Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis.”**
grounding.inference: Because the candidate prompt added a named preservation section, refining that section is a direct place to implement a more constrained, context-aware guard.
grounding.constraints: The quoted line shows the section exists but does not provide its full wording or the exact rules it contained; inspect `candidate/prompts/Narrative/` and the diff to design precise edits.

grounding.claim: The candidate prompt failed to preserve the intended editorial hierarchy: company identity and audience were subordinated while orchestration became central.
grounding.sourceEvidence: Candidate outputs were readable and coherent, but consistently subordinated company identity and audience scope while making orchestration the central positioning.
grounding.inference: This explicit failure mode supports a description that proposes treating technical explanations as subordinate and protecting company-level primacy in the guard.
grounding.constraints: This observation derives from the three candidate runs in this experiment; it demonstrates consistent regression in this dataset but is not a universal guarantee across different inputs, model backends, or future conditions.

grounding.claim: The practical implementers for these edits are the people who author and maintain the Narrative prompts and the pipeline that runs them.
grounding.sourceEvidence: The complete baseline and candidate prompts are saved under `baseline/prompts/Narrative/` and `candidate/prompts/Narrative/`.
grounding.inference: Because the prompts are repository artifacts in those paths, the relevant audience is prompt authors, owners, and pipeline engineers who maintain and deploy those files.
grounding.constraints: The source locations imply roles but do not name personnel; assign specific owners from project repo governance when scheduling work.

grounding.claim: Refinement is required because the candidate performed worse and introduced unsupported claims, failing critical gates.
grounding.sourceEvidence: Candidate was worse on mean score for both Narrative and Compose, failed the orchestration hierarchy and factual restraint gates in every run, and introduced regressions.
grounding.inference: The experiment summary directly links the candidate change to measurable negative outcomes and rule failures, justifying a targeted revision of the preservation rule rather than broader unrelated changes.
grounding.constraints: The experiment used three runs per condition and a single model alias; while results are internally consistent, they remain subject to model variability and limited-sample uncertainty.

grounding.claim: Concrete artifacts exist to develop and validate the refined guard and its tests.
grounding.sourceEvidence: Full console logs, extracted Narrative outputs, and final Compose outputs are saved under this experiment's `baseline/outputs/` and `candidate/outputs/`.
grounding.inference: The archived outputs and the prompt diff provide reproducible test vectors and traces to validate whether a refined guard prevents the observed regressions.
grounding.constraints: Artifacts are archived but the experiment notes limitations (no seed/temperature control, small sample size, possible provider alias backend changes) that affect how definitive validation will be across environments.
